clue.text: Old man confining most of rest in open space

indicators.note: the old man's letters hold the other piece inside them, as a cell confines a prisoner

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it bar its final letter here

parts.note: to laze is to rest idly

explanation.surface: An elderly man keeps lounging about in a public square.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square or open area in a town, typically paved.

clue.text: Controversial staff correspondence showing change of heart about Conservative

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod

indicators.note: the altered word goes round the Conservative's letter
the heart of the word for correspondence, its two middle letters, is altered by being swapped round

parts.note: mail is letters and correspondence

explanation.surface: Office letters about a Tory defector stir up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing change of heart' swaps the middle two letters, giving MIAL; 'about' wraps that round C to make MICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing is combative and argumentative, so it is controversial by nature.

clue.text: Gas power almost failed — almost

indicators.note: almost the whole word: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: arm means power or authority, as in the long arm of the law

indicators.note: again almost the whole word, losing its final letter

parts.note: gone can mean failed or finished, as in a gone business

explanation.surface: A power cut left the gas supply nearly dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, an inert noble gas found in the air.

clue.text: Benign power supply taken under a road

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is taken under comes below the earlier pieces

parts.note: MI stands for the M1, Britain's first motorway
a cable carries electric power

explanation.surface: A harmless electricity line has been laid beneath a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London-to-Leeds motorway; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and good-natured, close in sense to benign or kindly.

clue.text: Newspaper, perhaps, is about to back electronic device

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a body, a newspaper being one example

indicators.note: to back means to go backwards, so the word for about is read in reverse

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A paper is said to be backing some gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic organiser is a pocket gadget for diaries and contacts, the forerunner of the smartphone.

clue.text: It's my fault henhouses won't open

indicators.note: a word that won't open has no opening letter

parts.note: coops are cages for hens

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that the hen-house doors are stuck shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation of someone admitting a small blunder of their own.

clue.text: Oxford exam taking care of teacher training initially? My word

parts.note: Greats is the Oxford final exam in classics (Literae Humaniores)
c/o, written CO, is the abbreviation for care of on an address

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an Oxford exam that tests teacher training?
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T and T from 'teacher training'; 'taking' only links GREATS to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Scott is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like the interjection my word.

clue.text: Active amount of computer storage dropped in river

indicators.note: the storage letters are dropped into the river's name

parts.note: the Nile is the African river
MB is short for megabyte

explanation.surface: Someone lively has lost a computer memory stick in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble means quick and agile in movement, so lively and active.

clue.text: Drive out of capital of Turkey, chasing a great deal for the tourist

indicators.note: what chases comes after, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a sight can mean a lot, as in a sight better

indicators.note: the letter goes out of the word for drive

parts.note: to steer is to drive a vehicle

indicators.note: the capital letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A tourist drives out of Ankara, Turkey's capital, after a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Turkey' looks like Ankara but is just T; 'out of' removes it from STEER, leaving SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer visits famous places for pleasure, which is what a tourist does.

clue.text: Senior academic ignoring last page in book

indicators.note: the word's last letter is ignored

parts.note: a rector heads some colleges and Scottish universities

explanation.surface: A college head skips the final page of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf.

clue.text: Tip in gale at sea requires loading of program

indicators.note: the jumble takes the program loaded into it
at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: Advice on sailing in a storm needs a piece of software installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' jumbles the fodder into LAGNIE; 'requires loading of' slots the program into it before the final E. 'Tip' means a gratuity, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagniappe, a Louisiana word, is a small extra given free, like a gratuity or tip.

clue.text: Seasonal visitors beginning to congregate? Very good

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men who visit the infant Jesus, part of the Christmas season

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Christmas visitors start to gather: how lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is informal British praise meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Crazy graduate turned murderer

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: turned round, so the murderer's name reads backwards

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A deranged graduate became a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maniac can be used as an adjective meaning wildly mad or frenzied.

clue.text: Landed, rolling over in fight, producing knife

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or argument

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word round

parts.note: lit is a past tense of light, meaning landed, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A man fell, tumbled over in a scuffle and drew a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' is lit, as a bird lights on a branch; 'rolling over' gives TIL, which 'in' places after the first letter of the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Battered piano, missing note, embodying something obliterating musical form

indicators.note: the jumble holds the other piece in its body
battered means knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the word is missing the note's letter

parts.note: an eraser rubs out and obliterates marks

explanation.surface: A damaged piano, a key missing, has something wrecking a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops N to leave PIAO; 'Battered' rearranges that as OPIA; 'embodying' takes the rubber in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera seria is the serious, heroic style of Italian opera, a genre or form of music.

clue.text: Swims with speed where pipes run

parts.note: crawls means swims front crawl
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A swimmer does front crawl fast where water pipes flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawl space is a low gap under a floor or roof where services such as plumbing are laid.

clue.text: Taking away damaged bud in effect

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the word for effect

parts.note: in action means in effect or operation

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are spoilt, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Effectively, a damaged flower bud is being removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in effect' reads as one phrase but splits: 'damaged' gives BDU, and 'in' places it after the first letter of the word for effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction is the act of carrying someone off, a forcible taking away.

clue.text: Enthusiast cut trial recording

indicators.note: cut means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: a demon is a keen enthusiast, as in a demon for work

explanation.surface: A keen fan edits down a test recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a rough sample recording made to show what a band or song can do.

clue.text: Rash oaths very out of place

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are not where they belong, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Swearing very much in the wrong setting is reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhasty means acting too fast without thought, which is what rash means.

clue.text: A brief furore about unexciting idea from above?

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about the other
a brief word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: a fuss is a furore or commotion
flat means dull or unexciting

explanation.surface: A short-lived fuss over a dull idea that seems to come from on high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' leaves FUS; 'about' wraps it round the dull word, which sits after the first F.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflatus is divine inspiration, a creative impulse thought to come from heaven, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Disorder putting off old woman and another woman

indicators.note: putting off means sending away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a malady is an illness or disorder
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An illness making Mum drop one woman for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite word for a woman.

clue.text: To live in support of church involves routine strength

indicators.note: the word for live involves, takes in, the other letters

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a rut is a dull routine
for means in support of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Living to back the church brings a dull, strenuous routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' puts the routine inside the word for live, making BRUTE; 'church' is CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Brute force is sheer physical strength used without skill or subtlety.

clue.text: Opening a University? It's more than a piece of cake

definitions.text: It's more than a piece of cake

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A university entrance exam: anything but easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece of cake' suggests something easy; the definition means a whole rich cake, not just a slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a large elaborate cream cake, served whole rather than as a mere slice.

clue.text: Support intention to retain singular old expression

parts.note: an arch supports a structure above it

indicators.note: the word for intention keeps the singular letter inside it

parts.note: an aim is an intention
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Backing a plan to keep a single dated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is a word or phrase no longer in everyday use, such as forsooth.

clue.text: A plan to get rid of electric current in upper floor

indicators.note: the current's letters are got rid of from the plan's

parts.note: a tactic is a plan or scheme
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A scheme to remove the electricity supply on the top floor.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room or storey just under the roof of a house.

clue.text: Problem with lighting installed in grand church

indicators.note: lighting is installed inside, so these letters go in the middle

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
lit means lighting up or illuminated

explanation.surface: Trouble with the new lights put in a great cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden minor fault or malfunction, a small problem.

clue.text: Introduction of hike in rent is an irritation

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for rent

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bringing in a rent increase is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' reads as money paid for housing; here it means torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in one's side is a persistent annoyance, so thorn alone means an irritation.

clue.text: Limits to using lavatory? Nasty

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from both words

explanation.surface: Restrictions on toilet use? How horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean hostile or threatening, as in an ugly mood, which is nasty.

clue.text: Fifth journey is a load of rubbish

parts.note: a trip is a journey
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The fifth trip was a complete waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, cow's stomach as food, is also slang for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Strangely, this rogue is not like a rogue

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd order, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Oddly, this villain behaves unlike a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright and virtuous, the opposite of a scoundrel.

clue.text: Dodgy account receiving 1000 yen sparks defiance

indicators.note: the jumble receives the letter inside it
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A suspicious bank account taking in a large yen deposit provokes defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges the fodder as CONTUAC; 'receiving' takes the thousand in after its fifth letter, and the yen's letter ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumacy is stubborn refusal to obey authority, especially a court: wilful defiance.

clue.text: Edges of Selsey beach may be described thus

parts.note: the town's name pictured by its outer letters alone shows one letter and another, which spoken as a phrase runs together into the answer

explanation.surface: A beach at Selsey, a Sussex seaside town, would be described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as S AND Y: those two letters are the edges of 'Selsey', so the answer describes the clue's own wordplay as well as a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy describes a shore covered in sand, as many beaches are.
